walkthroughs.body_html:
Kennedy raised US 'advisors' from 800 in 1960 to 16,000 by 1963.

Diem's Catholic regime persecuted Buddhists. After monk Thich Quang Duc's self-immolation, the US backed a coup. Diem was killed on 2 November 1963 — three weeks before Kennedy.

In August 1964 the Gulf of Tonkin Incident — disputed shots at US destroyers — let Johnson pass the Tonkin Resolution.

Operation Rolling Thunder (1965-68) dropped more bombs than fell in all of WWII. US troops peaked at 540,000 in 1968. Napalm and Agent Orange devastated villages and forests.

On 30-31 January 1968 the Viet Cong hit over 100 cities during the Tet New Year truce.

The US embassy in Saigon was briefly stormed. Militarily the VC lost — but TV coverage convinced US opinion the war was unwinnable. Walter Cronkite called it a stalemate. LBJ withdrew from the 1968 election.
